# core/rows.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/rows.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Tables of fixed-size rows in one `Buf`.

A kernel often keeps a table as one buffer of words with a row of
`stride` words per entry (a process table, per-process descriptor
rows), and indexes it as `get(t, id * stride + field)`. `rows_grow`
makes such a table longer without touching the code that indexes it:
the old rows keep their place and contents, and every new row is all
zeros (make 0 the "free" value of the field that says whether a row is
in use). When memory runs out it returns false and leaves the table as
it was, so a kernel can answer ENOMEM or EAGAIN instead of stopping.

What is proved: the new length is the old one plus `k` rows, every old
word is unchanged, and every new word is 0. Each fact is one quantifier
over word positions, with no multiplication inside, so the proofs hold
in programs whose other invariants make Z3's job harder (see
tests/pass/core_all_counting.bastio). A version that copied a
template row needed a nested quantifier over row and field, which did
not prove in such a program (BastiOS's kernel).

`import "core/rows.bastio";`

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`rows_grow`](#rows_grow) | Grows `t` by `k` rows of `stride` words, all zero. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `rows_grow`

```bastio
fn rows_grow(t: &mut Buf, stride: u64, k: u64) -> bool
  requires 0 < stride
  ensures result ==> len(t) == len(old(t)) + k * stride
  ensures !result ==> len(t) == len(old(t))
  ensures forall j: u64 :: j < len(old(t)) ==> get(t, j) == get(old(t), j)
  ensures result ==> (forall j: u64 :: len(old(t)) <= j && j < len(t) ==> get(t, j) == 0)
```

Grows `t` by `k` rows of `stride` words, all zero. Returns false, with
`t` unchanged, when memory runs out (or when the new length would pass
2^60).

Example:

```bastio
// A table of 3-word rows, starting empty.
let mut t = alloc(0);
if !rows_grow(&mut t, 3, 2) {
  free(t);
  return 1;   // out of memory: the table is unchanged
}
assert len(t) == 6 && get(t, 4) == 0;   // two rows, all zero
t = set(t, 3, 7);                        // row 1, field 0
if rows_grow(&mut t, 3, 2) {
  assert len(t) == 12 && get(t, 3) == 7;   // old rows keep their words
}
free(t);
```
